story_type: disabled sailboat at night in 15-foot seas far offshore, child aboard, helicopter hoists
hook: A 4-year-old girl was on this sailboat, at night, in 15-foot seas.
narration: A four year old girl was on this sailboat, at night, in fifteen foot seas.
The forty seven foot sailboat Panache was headed from Annapolis to the U.S. Virgin Islands.
About one hundred seventy five miles from Bermuda, it lost steering and propulsion.
The sailors called the Coast Guard on a satellite phone.
An HC-130 crew marked the boat's position and guided in a Jayhawk helicopter from Elizabeth City, North Carolina.
This was filmed with an infrared camera, which sees heat, so it works in total darkness.
The wind was blowing more than thirty knots.
[short pause] The mast whipped back and forth as the boat rolled under the helicopter.
One by one, the crew lifted everyone off the boat.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted all six to safety, the four year old girl among them.
title: 4-year-old on a sailboat in 15-foot seas
description:
On Nov. 16, 2008, a Coast Guard MH-60J Jayhawk crew from Elizabeth City, N.C., hoisted five adults and a 4-year-old girl from the disabled 47-foot sailboat Panache, 175 nautical miles west-northwest of Bermuda, in 15-foot seas and winds over 30 knots.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video, Air Station Elizabeth City, N.C., via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/313727/panache-hoist

facts.claim: Five adults and a 4-year-old girl hoisted 175 nm WNW of Bermuda after the sailboat became disabled
facts.source_quote: A Coast Guard helicopter crew hoisted five adults and one 4-year-old girl to safety Sunday, Nov. 16, 2008, 175 nautical miles west-northwest of Bermuda after their sailboat became disabled.

facts.claim: 47-foot Panache lost steering and propulsion en route Annapolis to St. Thomas, called by satellite phone
facts.source_quote: The sailors aboard the 47-foot sailboat, Panache, lost steering and propulsion while transiting to St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands, from Annapolis, Md., and contacted the Coast Guard via satallite phone requesting assistance.

facts.claim: HC-130J marked the position and vectored the Elizabeth City Jayhawk, FLIR video
facts.source_quote: An HC-130J Hercules aircraft crew from Elizabeth City, N.C., marked the position of the sailboat, vectored the Elizabeth City MH-60J Jayhawk helicopter in and used a Forward Looking Infrared camera to capture this video.
During the hoist, the winds were more than 30 knots and the seas were 15 feet.
